title: ST-Veto: Spatio-Temporal Token Veto for Diffusion MLLMs via Taylor Prediction and Visual Grounding
claim: Standard decoding commits high-confidence but ungrounded or unstable tokens and errs; adding stability and grounding vetoes yields correct output.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, top-to-bottom timesteps, veto callout insets on right
description: A question banner at the top shows a photo of a man cutting a cake with the prompt 'What is happening in the image?'. Below, two panels are separated by a vertical black line. The left panel, (a) Base, shows four rows of token boxes at timesteps t-3, t-2, t-1 and t. Blue boxes mark newly unmasked tokens, such as 'eats' and 'fork'. Captions under each row explain the choices. The panel ends with the incorrect output 'A man eats cake with a fork', marked with a red X. The right panel, (b) ST-Veto, repeats the same rows. Red crossed-out ghost tokens 'eats' and 'loves' are vetoed, with dashed lines linking them to two inset bar-chart callouts. The callouts show image-attention and Taylor-residual drops. The panel ends with the correct output 'A man cuts cake with a knife', marked with a green check.
caption: Overview of our work. The base decoder unmasks tokens according to current-step confidence, whereas ST-Veto applies temporal-stability and visual-grounding checks before committing tokens to the denoising trajectory.
abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) achieve strong reasoning with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting but incur high sequential-generation cost, error accumulation, and limited self-correction. Diffusion Multimodal Large Language Models (dMLLMs) unmask tokens in an order-agnostic process, improving efficiency and enabling iterative refinement, yet their reasoning and how to enhance it remain underexplored. We propose a training-free method, Spatio-Temporal Token Veto (ST-Veto), which leverages the ability to observe all token positions at each diffusion step. Rather than relying only on current-step confidence, ST-Veto vetoes temporally unstable tokens via second-order Taylor prediction of confidence dynamics and filters weakly grounded tokens using image-attention mass, swapping them with safer candidates. Across multiple dMLLMs and multimodal reasoning benchmarks, ST-Veto consistently outperforms standard decoding policies and prior VLM reasoning methods, improving accuracy by up to 9% with no additional training or generation cost. Analyses show that ST-Veto steers generation toward higher-confidence, better-grounded paths.
